cards.text: We're in Zechariah the prophet (Zechariah 1:1), and here comes the burden of the word of the LORD concerning Israel. It comes from the LORD, who stretches out the heavens, lays the foundation of the earth and forms the spirit of man within him. And I'm known as "the guy with the mustache."
Now the LORD speaks about Jerusalem and all the peoples around her. These are the peoples who are coming against her.

cards.question: The peoples around Jerusalem are coming against her. The LORD makes Jerusalem a cup of ___ for them.
When the siege comes, only Jerusalem is surrounded and Judah is left alone.

cards.text: On that day, all the nations of the earth gather against Jerusalem, and the LORD makes her a heavy stone for all the peoples. It's like when your friend swears his dresser is "light" and you actually believe him.

cards.question: Jerusalem is a heavy stone for all the peoples. What happens to everyone who tries to heave it away?

answers.text: They will break it in pieces

cards.text: On that day, the LORD strikes every horse with panic and every rider with madness. I know that look, friend: that was ME the first time my mixer jumped to high speed.

cards.question: The LORD strikes the horses of the nations with blindness, and He leaves the house of Judah to fight alone.

cards.text: Then the leaders of Judah say something in their hearts. They say the people of Jerusalem are their strength.

cards.question: The leaders of Judah say the people of Jerusalem are their strength. Why?

answers.text: Because the LORD of Hosts is their God
Because Jerusalem has the strongest walls
Because the nations have all gone home

cards.text: Then the LORD makes the clans of Judah like a firepot in a woodpile, like a flaming torch among the sheaves. Friend, I once let parchment paper slide too close to my oven, so I know EXACTLY how this goes.

cards.question: The clans of Judah are like a firepot in a woodpile. What happens to the peoples around them?

answers.text: They are consumed on the right and the left
They put out the fire of Judah
They run to Judah for shelter

cards.question: While the fire of Judah spreads among the peoples, the people of Jerusalem remain secure.

cards.text: Now the LORD talks about the house of David, King David's royal family. He also talks about the people of Jerusalem and the tents of Judah.

cards.question: The LORD doesn't want the glory of the house of David and the people of Jerusalem to be greater than that of Judah. So who does He save first?
When the LORD defends the people of Jerusalem, even the weakest among them will be like David.

cards.text: The WEAKEST one, friend! In my bakery that's me after carrying one tray of cookies, and even I would be like DAVID. And the house of David will be like God, like the angel of the LORD going before them.

cards.question: So on that day, the LORD sets out to ___ all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

cards.text: Then the LORD says He will pour something out on the house of David and the people of Jerusalem.

cards.question: What does the LORD pour out on the house of David and the people of Jerusalem?

answers.text: A spirit of grace and prayer

cards.text: And then the LORD says they "will look on Me, the One they have pierced." When a soldier pierces Jesus' side at the cross, John quotes this very Scripture (John 19:34-37).

cards.question: With a spirit of grace and prayer poured out on them, they look on the One they have pierced and ___ for Him.
The house of David and the people of Jerusalem mourn for the One they have pierced as for an only child, and grieve bitterly for Him as for a firstborn son.

cards.text: On that day, the wailing in Jerusalem will be as great as the wailing of Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo. That's not a couple of sniffles, friend.
The land mourns, each clan on its own, and their wives too. The list names the house of David, the house of Nathan, the house of Levi and the clan of Shimei, and then all the remaining clans.
Then, on that day, a fountain is opened to the house of David and the people of Jerusalem. After all those tears, friend, here comes the turn.

cards.question: The fountain is opened to the house of David and the people of Jerusalem to cleanse them from ___ and impurity.

cards.text: The LORD of Hosts says He will erase the names of the idols from the land. Friend, my eraser can't even get a smudge of dough off a recipe card, and the LORD erases whole NAMES.

cards.question: Once the LORD erases the names of the idols, they will still be remembered in the land.

cards.text: He also removes the prophets and the spirit of impurity from the land. And if anyone still prophesies, his own father and mother, the ones who bore him, step in.

cards.question: A man is still prophesying in the land. What do his father and mother say he has done?

answers.text: Spoken falsely in the name of the LORD
Turned away from working the land
Stolen from the house of the LORD

cards.text: They tell him he shall not remain alive, and when he prophesies, they pierce him through. On that day, every prophet who prophesies will be ashamed of his vision.

cards.question: On that day, an ashamed prophet will no longer put on a hairy cloak in order to deceive.

cards.text: No more hairy cloak to fool anybody. Now listen to how he describes himself, because friend, that résumé just got a FULL rewrite.

cards.question: How does the ashamed prophet describe himself now?

answers.text: Not a prophet but a servant who works the land
Not a prophet but a priest in the temple
Not a prophet but a merchant from Tarshish

cards.question: Someone asks the ashamed prophet about the wounds on his chest. What does he say?

answers.text: He received them in the house of his friends
He received them while working in the fields
He received them in a battle long ago

cards.text: Then the tone shifts hard. The LORD of Hosts calls a sword to awake against His Shepherd, against the man who is His Companion.

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts says to strike the Shepherd. What happens to the sheep?

answers.text: They will find a new shepherd

cards.text: And the LORD says He will turn His hand against the little ones. On the night Jesus is arrested, He quotes the line about the Shepherd and the scattered sheep, telling His disciples they will all fall away (Matthew 26:31, 47-50).

cards.question: In all the land, the LORD says many will be cut off and perish, but a ___ will be left in it.

cards.text: That third, the LORD will bring through the fire. Friend, I've stood in front of a hot oven for YEARS, and I still jump every time that door swings open.

cards.question: Why does the LORD bring that third through the fire?

answers.text: To refine them like silver and test them like gold
To burn them away from the land for good
To punish them and then leave them behind

cards.question: The LORD says that when the refined third call on His name, He will answer them.

cards.text: And then the best part, friend: the LORD will say, 'They are My people,' and they will say, 'The LORD is our God.' Out of the fire and right into the family.

findings.problem: The setup gives the baker no basis for inferring the unseen image of drunkenness. The blank therefore asks for wording the baker has not seen rather than a meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the exclamation about the weakest one, the bakery joke, and the statement about the house of David. That exceeds the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Jesus and John appear for the first time in the walkthrough without a simple identification of who they are. Jesus is only named, and John is introduced merely as someone who quotes the Scripture.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The summary of this clan list goes through every named item: David, Nathan, Levi and Shimei, followed by the remaining clans. A short summary could convey the clan-by-clan mourning with one standout detail instead of reproducing the whole list.

rule.text: He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item. He can name a standout detail the text gives if it helps the stretch stick.

findings.problem: No earlier card supplies the two-thirds and one-third division, and saying only that many will perish does not make third inferable over half or tenth. The blank is a luck-based request for an unseen numerical detail rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The question relies on "that third" pointing back to earlier cards. Standing alone, it does not identify the group as the third left in the land.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
